item.title: Morning Coffee: Hedge fund recruiter on $800k is unhappy in Hong Kong. Goldman Sachs' rehired partner was a good buy
item.description:
How much do you earn as a senior business development professional who recruits portfolio managers (PM) for a hedge fund? Based upon a recently filed court document in Hong Kong, you won't get as much as an actual PM, but you will still get a lot.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Reporting on the filing, Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-27/hedge-fund-verition-sued-by-ex-asia-business-development-head?taid=6ae02fe408444f00015c8429&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>notes that Elizabeth Xiang spent nearly five years working for Verition, the friendlyish multistrategy hedge fund. Xiang was Asia-Pacific head of business development there and her court filing says Verition’s headcount in the region grew from four to 87 during her time. Thirty PMs were hired locally and Xiang says she was responsible for 27 of them.
As a reward for her efforts, Xiang says she was paid a salary of around US$200k in 2025, plus a bonus of roughly $600k. When she joined in 2021, her salary was $150k, and she says her bonus rose every year. Times were good.
In late 2025, though, Xiang's mother in China had a cancer relapse and she spent early 2026 travelling to and fro to care for her. Xiang says Verition started a new project to map portfolio managers in the APAC market without telling her. Then she says the fund suddenly fired her in June, citing “failure to consistently follow reasonable management instructions,” “inconsistent follow-through” and “ongoing communication concerns with internal and external stakeholders.” Xiang claims she was fired because she took time off to care for her mother and because Verition didn't want to pay her 2026 bonus.
Verition didn't comment for Bloomberg's article. We have contacted the fund for comment. The account of Xiang's employment and firing is therefore drawn from her own perspective. Bloomberg says she plans to file for discrimination too. Working as a bus dev in hedge funds is good, until it's not.
Separately, it's not really so long ago that Nick Giovanni </news/goldman-sachs-partner-retired-return>galloped back to Goldman Sachs after an eight month holiday and three and a half years at Instacart, during which the company completed a $660m IPO and Giovanni presumably became quite rich.
A lesser man might have retired at this point but as we noted in February, Giovanni is very passionate about being a banker and has said things like: “Advising founders, executives and boards is what I love to do."
This is fortunate for Goldman Sachs, because yesterday the bank won yet another prestigious lead left position on a key 2026 IPO, this time Anthropic's. Giovanni and Jung Min - a Goldman TMT banker friendly with NVIDIA - appear to be the Goldman bankers responsible for this.
Giovanni's passion is less fortunate for Morgan Stanley, which has once again </news/space-x-ipo-goldman-sachs-morgan-stanley> been relegated to the position of stabilisation agent. This is contrary to earlier reports </news/anthropic-ipo-morgan-stanley-goldman-sachs> that Morgan Stanley was going to be lead left this time after sadly ceding the position to Goldman on the SpaceX IPO. It may also be contrary to Morgan Stanley's own expectations. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-26/goldman-s-210-billion-day-of-deals-driven-by-ai-financing-fever>notes that Morgan Stanley led Anthropic's $15bn revolving credit line. Its bankers may have expected to get prime position on the IPO as a result. It was not to be; Giovanni is too passionate.
Meanwhile...
Anthropic has seven co-founders. They will each be worth more than $13bn. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-26/anthropic-s-seven-founders-are-worth-more-than-13-billion-each?taid=6adf97821579270001ce0d28&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Revenue per employee at Anthropic is over $6.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $1.4 million as of September 30, 2025. (Anthropic prospectus, marked up) <https://docs.pe.finance/anthropic-s1/>
Citadel Securities is getting a bigger India office. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-26/ken-griffin-s-citadel-securities-to-expand-india-office>
Balyasny hired Matti Konsala from Citi for equities algo trading. (Trade) <https://www.thetradenews.com/balyasny-am-adds-citi-equities-algo-trader-to-systematic-trading-team/>
Capula is opening an Athens office and wants someone to set it up. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-26/capula-explores-greek-office-in-move-following-rokos-millennium?utm_source=website&utm_medium=share&utm_campaign=twitter>
AI could do the work of credit traders. Credit investors and traders are already asking Agentic BondGPT to alert them when a CCC bond trades more than 50 basis points wide from its prior day close. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-26/ai-agents-seen-taking-credit-trading-work-from-humans-over-time?srnd=phx-markets>
Microsoft is offering 60,000 employees a great chance to become unemployed. “This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support.” Standard severance will be paid. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-26/microsoft-to-offer-buyouts-to-60-000-workers-in-latest-cost-cut?taid=6adf907bd939c80001a7c6d3&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Ondřej Surý fixed the PHP flaws without being paid. He did get $10k in donations. (BBC) <https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw30ejqljl43o>
No one is leaving Deloitte either. The voluntary attrition rate there for the 2025/26 financial year was 10.3%, according to the pay report. That’s slightly up from 10% in 2025 and 9.4% in 2024, but below its pre-pandemic level of 12.8% in 2020 and 14.8% in 2019. (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/deloittes-uk-pay-report-shines-spotlight-on-attrition-ceo-pay-and-diversity-d408653e>
The tragic tale of the man who exposed Howard Lutnick's links to Jeffrey Epstein. “I’ve lost all my money, my wife and I are separated, and I’m in danger of having my home repossessed. Speaking out has devastated my life.” Two months later he was dead. The FCA is accused of failing to protect him. (Banker) <https://www.thebanker.com/content/f16e27fb-e461-4853-8128-f088ff00dc29>

item.title: HSBC may increase bonuses. Hong Kong bankers may get them
item.description:
HSBC results are out. After what the bank describes as a “strong” third quarter in which profits across the bank rose 32% as a more “simplified and agile” HSBC emerged, HSBC is considering increasing bonuses. Based upon Q3 results, lucky bankers and traders may receive them.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Revenues in HSBC’s Hong Kong corporate and institutional bank (CIB) rose 24% year-on-year in the third quarter, versus a paltry 6% increase in the non-ring fenced bank in the UK where the London bankers and traders sit. Revenues in the Middle East, excluding Saudi Arabia, fell 2%. Profits in the Hong Kong CIB were up 70%, versus a drop of 5% in the UK once unusually high costs relating to last year’s restructuring are removed.
HSBC has indicated that it will be paying bonuses </news/hsbc-bonuses-2026> proportionate to performance now that it's liberated from the EU bonus cap. Last year, the average bonus for its material risk takers was $819k. This year, CFO Pam Kaur said the bank is considering increasing variable pay (bonuses) if strong performance continues. Pre-tax profit in the CIB is up 16% year-on-year across the first nine months as a whole.
Kaur said that the bank's surprise decision </news/hscb-closure-europe-us-job-cuts>to simplify itself by pulling out of M&A and ECM in Europe and the US and to focus on the Middle East and Asia is going well. <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/hsbc-cfo-says-dealmaking-pivot-to-asia-and-middle-east-has-paid-off-dfbacbda?mod=homepage>“We are working around on around 70 live IPO mandates, of which more than 40 are in Hong Kong, and with over 25, we have a sponsor role,” she declared.
HSBC doesn’t break out performance in fixed income and equities sales and trading, or the performance of M&A, ECM or DCM bankers. Excluding FX trading, which has been shunted into wholesale transaction banking, sales and trading revenues at HSBC were up an impressive 69% in Q3. Investment banking revenues rose by a less impressive 12%, what with European and US banking closures last year.
Kaur said HSBC won't make a final decision on higher bonuses until January. When she does, who will get them? Maybe FX traders, whom Kaur says have been thriving in the transaction bank, where FX revenues rose 19% in Q3. Maybe Hong Kong bankers with all their mandates. Maybe Hong Kong traders. Maybe people in financing and prime broking, whom HSBC said are thriving with "increased volumes and wider margins”. Maybe even bankers and traders in London and the US. On a nine month basis, profit growth at the US CIB has outperformed the other regions and the Middle East and Asia don't look quite so impressive.
Last year, there was some whinging from HSBC employees about the allocation of bonuses in London. There were also job cuts a few weeks before bonuses were announced. HSBC's London bankers and traders also like to complain that costs are disproportionately allocated to their entity.
HSBC hasn’t finished cost cutting. It still plans to cut $100m of costs in the fourth quarter. Once that's done, it will have finally achieved its $2bn annualised target. Hooray.

item.title: "Hedge funds hired too many morons" and other unpopular opinions as the industry pukes PMs
item.description:
Spare a thought for the hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>. As we reported last week, both macro </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up>and credit funds </news/european-high-yield> have been flooding the street with newly unwanted talent. Goldman Sachs' prime brokerage </news/prime-broking-banks-2026> desk said <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-23/hedge-funds-log-widest-daily-drawdown-since-covid-in-stock-rout> last week that funds have also experienced one of their broadest equities declines since the COVID pandemic. All is pain.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Portfolio managers </news/finance/portfolio-manager-job-hedge-fund-lifestyle> are suffering. A chart has been circulating on X <https://x.com/AndreasSteno/status/2113651945122443273?s=20>suggesting 100 PMs are out so far this month, versus 40 in September and closer to 20 before that. Hedge fund headhunters say the number of people out of the market is enormous.
The reasons for the PM exits vary by strategy, but most were stopped out after making losses that exceed their risk limits. In credit, there are issues with weak covenants, regulatory intervention and rising rates. </news/european-high-yield>In macro, leveraged trades on French government bonds blew up. </news/european-high-yield>In equities, tech stocks sold off. Even multistrategy funds, supposedly insulated against issues from individual strategies were down 1.9% on Thursday according to Goldman data.
Not everyone is sympathetic. As hedge funds have increased their assets under management, headcount at leading funds has increased substantially </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-hiring>with many new hires drawn from banks. ADV forms indicate that 2,000 people were added last year alone. Some in the industry say funds have been scraping the barrel.
"Hedge funds hired too many morons," says one US portfolio manager. "A lot of people in funds are now very unimpressive," he adds. "There are a lot of clowns who were just long bonds and who have been killed."
Instead of PMs in funds originating trade ideas, he says the model has reversed. "The sellside pitches the ideas and people start to get in on a trade. Then other banks keep repeating the same ideas, and so buyside people keep getting in the same trade until it’s too crowded."
It ends in a situation where the majority of the buyside is on a similar trade until something happens to reverse it, he says. "And then they can’t get out fast enough because they don’t have enough understanding of the fundamentals and factors that causing problems to that trade."
As funds have scrambled to increase headcount, he says they've hired too many juniors from banks. But banks themselves already lost their best senior traders to hedge funds years ago and the juniors being hired have lacked guidance from talented traders. "There are no mentors left on the sellside to coach juniors," says another portfolio manager.
Coupled with the fact that the job of a portfolio manager is very different to the job of a trader on a desk in a bank, this has contributed to the blow-ups, say observers. "It is a very different world being a market making junior on a desk to trying to trade against the spread. You are not just doing trades and hedging against a book but are exposed to market moves and the dislocations that have happened this year," says one industry insider.
All of this implies that portfolio managers leaving now will find it hard to get new roles. Many are on non-competes anyway. Some have only recently been hired and are on guarantees.
Some in the market strongly disagree with the framing above, though. One young PM tells us the losses and stopping-outs have nothing to do with PM ability and everything to do with the growing size of funds. Freddie Parks, head of Goldman Sachs' prime broking team, said in September that $500bn had flowed into multistrategy funds in the previous 12 months. </news/goldman-sachs-md-says-multistrategy-hedge-funds-may-yet-need-many-more-p-ms>
"The real cause is that hedge fund AUM have exploded, so everything is more crowded and markets can’t absorb that much liquidity," says the young PM. It's not the fault of the young traders hired from banks. If anything, he says they are very risk averse because they weren't taught about real risk-taking in banks. Some funds charge PMs for the capital allocated to them, creating pressure to put capital to work even in difficult markets.
At some point, funds will need to hire new people. There are rumours of non-competes being shortened to facilitate this. Some of those now out of the market will have to come back in a different guise, says Richard Averill at Waterline Compensation, <https://waterlineeconomics.com/> which models hedge fund pay. "Most teams have a strategy that differentiates them from other PMs, but if your strategy no longer works, you don’t just have bad positions, you have a strategy that no longer makes sense."

item.title: Citi has picked up yet another Deutsche Bank MD. In LevFin, this time
item.description:
Some of the most iconic combinations in history need no introduction. Laurel and Hardy in America, Fry and Laurie in the UK. Enemies to lovers on Ao3. In finance, it seems to increasingly be “joined Citi” and “left Deutsche Bank”.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Ilir Hasi joined Citi in New York this month as a managing director </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds> (MD) in its Leveraged Finance (LevFin) team. He joined Citi from Deutsche Bank in the city, where he spent seven and a half years, and was made an MD in 2024 </news/deutsche-bank-s-new-managing-directors>. Hasi was at BMO Capital Markets before that. Citi did not respond to a request for comment.
LevFin has seen better days. US Treasury yields hit multi-decade highs in September, and equity and debt issuance slowed late in the third quarter. In July, asset management firm PIMCO warned <https://www.pimco.com/gb/en/insights/the-credit-market-lens-a-growing-divide-in-leveraged-finance> that distress is likely to rise in leveraged loans, even if the economy holds up, blaming the private credit fundraising boom (and the subsequent struggles of software companies in the AI world. High yield has suffered </news/european-high-yield> in particular.
Nonetheless, Citi has stacked up on LevFin talent, including from Deutsche Bank – Ludovic Ingelaere joined Citi from Deutsche in Paris as an MD in its LevFin team in July last year. It also hired Jenner Kizer </news/citi-hired-a-lev-fin-guy-from-deutsche-bank-and-he-is-moving-on> from Deutsche back in 2022. Citi has hired a lot of people </news/citi-hiring-deutsche-bank> from Deutsche Bank in general, recently - Citi's banking head, Vis Raghavan, said <https://www.wsj.com/finance/banking/the-outsider-trying-to-restore-citi-to-investment-banking-glory-b2802e99?st=z6UoP4&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink> back in 2024 about wanting to invest in the bank's financial sponsors team. Expanding his bank's LevFin abilities is part of that. The firm has hired sponsors bankers substantially, including recently - Antonio Iannella joined the firm as a sponsors MD in Milan earlier this month, for example.
LevFin can pay very well when the times are good. A compensation report from earlier this year from Prospect Rock Partners found that </news/the-best-leveraged-finance-m-ds-earn-the-most-now-directors-not-so-much> LevFin MDs earned $1.6m on average for their work in 2025, much higher than the rest of their investment banking peers, who earned an average of $1.1m in the same period. 2026 might be even better; Citi’s Q3 results a few weeks ago noted that a decline in debt capital markets </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm> revenue was “primarily” offset by a growth in leveraged finance revenue.

item.title: What to expect from the case study in a private credit interview
item.description:
If you want to work in a private credit </news/private-credit>fund in London, you may have encountered Richard Hoar.
Hoar is a director at recruitment firm Goodman Masson, who specialises in private credit </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-private-equity> jobs. He cut his teeth recruiting for middle and back office jobs in the early 2000s, but has “moved up the value chain.” So has the recruitment market, says Hoar.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
For all the bad press about redemptions from private credit funds and fraud-induced losses at the likes of Jefferies and Barclays, Hoar says private credit jobs retain their appeal. “It’s the buyside,” he explains. “You’re the principal, that’s more glamorous.”
While private equity funds provide capital that gives them a share in the equity of companies that are not publicly traded on exchanges, private credit funds make loans to companies that either can’t or don’t want to borrow in other ways. Private equity firms like to hire former M&A </news/get-a-job-in-ma> juniors; private credit firms like to hire former leveraged finance bankers.
Hoar says competition for places in private credit firms remains intense. “The funnel is sharp,” he says. Hundreds of people are filtered out after sending in CVs. 20-25 might get through to the first interview. 12 might get through to the second round interview. Six get through to the case study. Two get offers.
If you make it through to the case study, you are therefore doing well. Hoar says the case studies typically involve a presentation based around company accounts.
“You will have 3-4 hours to prepare the presentation and they will often put mistakes in there that they you want you to spot,” he says. The emphasis is on identifying errors in covenants and documentation that might make the deal too friendly towards the borrower, plus reasons why the fund might make a loss. You’ll be asked to produce a memorandum on the deal and will be interrogated on this, says Hoar.
How can you prepare? Make sure you’re familiar with covenants and loan documentation. Make sure you can read a balance sheet.
Make sure, too, that you are used to presenting and to defending your case. “They want to see that you have attention to detail, can tell a story and can handle yourself under pressure,” says Hoar. “There will often be a good cop- bad cop approach to see if you can still handle yourself and come up with the right answers when you’re under pressure.”

item.title: Morning Coffee: The most hardcore man in financial services defines four tiers of people. London bankers on £200k+ have new apprehension
item.description:
There are some intense people in financial services. Take Peter de Putron who runs electronic trading firm G-Research and whom the Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/bc6bba42-0b33-4825-a2c5-cff9b8f5c591?syn-25a6b1a6=1>says goes about in a hat and sunglasses indoors, gives no one his mobile number and can be "intense, direct and at times awkward" according to those who have met him.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
De Putron lives in Jersey and no one even seems to know what he looks like beyond that he is tall and blonde. Nik Storonsky </news/revolut-underperformance-nik-storonsky> at Revolut is also tall and blonde and is more familiar. But in his way, Storonsky is equally inscrutable.
In a new long interview <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hT_MAAwFLIc&t=2018s> with the Founders podcast, Storonsky revealed that he doesn't smile much, laughs less and looks quite tired. This might be because, by his own admission, he works 99.5% of the time and a typical week involves something like working from 9am to 9pm, seven days a week.
This leaves little time for kitesurfing or sailing around in yachts, but Storonsky doesn't seem to mind because he is a hypercompetitive person who is coming for Jamie Dimon's "dinner." This means retail banking, but also maybe investment banking too. Investment banking is "still very manual, still very expensive. I mean it’s all possible to make it all much cheaper as well. Why not?," Storonsky says.
It's not easy to work for Storonsky at Revolut. Millions applied last year and 0.15% got hired. </news/revolut-the-fintech-hiring-0-15-of-applicants-raised-pay>Storonsky can afford to be choosy. He says he ideally likes to hire people aged 25-30 who are in the top 1% of their peer group and that there is a "prime age," beyond which people probably become "less good."
The culture at Revolut is famously aggressive </news/2023/10/revolut-culture> and Storonsky seems cool with this as he pursues Dimon's dinner. He tells the Founders podcast there are four tiers of people:
"Self-guided people are like self-guided missiles... you don't even need to tell them what the goal is, they self-identify the goal and then they self-reach it." "
"People who are good but not excellent, you need to tell them the goal and then without any kind of iteration they will reach the goal."
"Average people, you tell them the goal and then you need to spend weekly iterations with them to direct them, to tell them what to do, and then they will reach the goal. So you spend management time. That's what I don't want."
"Below average people, you gave them the goal, you spend time with them and then most likely they will not hit the goal."
The trick is to hire people in the first tier. Then you can have lots of direct reports. "You just need to minimise management time spent on each of them," Storonsky explains.
If you self-define as a hardcore self-guided missile and like working 9-9-7, Storonsky will both hire you and stick up for you. He told the podcast that a VC investor wanted him to fire his best employee for being "too hardcore." - "I said no. That’s it,” Storonsky said. The VC then "stepped back."
Separately, if you are billionaire in the UK you have received a letter from the government and if you earn over £200k in the UK you should be apprehensive that you will receive one next.
The Sunday Times <https://www.thetimes.com/money/tax/article/hmrcs-letters-wealthy-reveal-assets-pzjrn50hm>reported that UK billionaires received a mysterious letter from Her Majesties Revenue and Customs (HMRC) calling them "customers" and asking them to reveal detailed information about their affairs, including the sources of their wealth and their future intentions. The letter can be seen in full here. <https://x.com/banthebbc/status/2114305612813316288?s=20>
HMRC's interest may not stop with billionaires. The Sunday Times says it's considering sending similar letters to people earning £200k who have £2m of assets.
“Who do these people think they are, the Stasi? This will only encourage more people to leave,” said one billionaire in receipt of the letter.
Meanwhile...
Ex-UK Goldman Sachs chief and Revolut board member Mike Sherwood is going to Jersey. (Sky) <https://news.sky.com/story/former-goldman-chief-sherwood-leaves-britain-amid-tax-hike-fears-13602963>
Barclays likes its equities traders now. It is "rebalancing" towards them and it's diverted capital away from macro towards prime. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-24/barclays-house-of-fixed-income-pins-future-growth-on-equities?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261024&utm_campaign=author_21061455>
Chris Wheeler and Daniel Dangoor, each of whom ran their own macro investing team at ExodusPoint, have left. Dangoor only joined from Goldman Sach in June. (Business Insider) <https://www.businessinsider.com/exoduspoint-macro-traders-out-2026-10>
Goldman Sachs says hedge funds had a terrible time Thursday, with their broadest losses since 2020. “For the first time since Covid, all three broad equity strategies fell more than 1% on the same day.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-23/hedge-funds-log-widest-daily-drawdown-since-covid-in-stock-rout>
It's a fine time to be a metals trader and Vitol is hiring more of them. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-24/metals-traders-reap-bonanza-with-another-year-of-record-profits?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261024&utm_campaign=author_22490032>
Deloitte is hiring 100 dealmakers in the north. (CityAM) <https://www.cityam.com/deloitte-to-create-100-new-jobs-with-launch-of-regional-deals-unit/>
Alvarez & Marsal is on a hiring spree and wants to recruit 20 “AI managing directors” and establish an “AI laboratory” in Spain. It already employs 1,700 people in the UK. (Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/business/companies-markets/article/alvarez-and-marsal-doubles-hiring-big-four-p6czf3b62>
Citi now has a license to set up its own Chinese securities unit and wants to be big in China. (Reuters) <https://www.reuters.com/world/china/citi-wins-licence-set-up-fully-owned-china-securities-unit-2026-10-23/>
A self-employed man repayed £40k of his student loan in the UK and it wasn't reflected in his balance. He contacted the student loans company and they told him could either repay what the system said he owed and wait for a refund or delay settlement until April, when it would have processed self-assessment payment data from HM Revenue & Customs. Then he started receiving huge bills for interest payments. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/49eca17a-3b4e-46e0-8691-417f679cc6b0?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
If you have man boobs you can get breast reduction surgery. (AirMail) <https://airmail.news/fitness/2026/10/coping-with-man-boobs?utm_content=look&utm_medium=email&utm_source=blast&utm_campaign=newsletter-3954>
400 people applied for a job as a barista. (BBC) <https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq369401rdx4o>
Gen Z want to work in cubicles. "I can’t really focus on my work, and I can’t get any privacy. I know people from my parents’ generation rave about having open, bright and airy spaces compared to cubicles, but it’s really a nightmare for me." (Metro) <https://metro.co.uk/2026/10/15/gen-z-want-this-90s-office-staple-revived-avoid-feeling-overstimulated-29707411/>
A recruiter who once had 11 staff now runs her company with AI agents. One spots new business from filings and announcements, one produces market intelligence on scarce skills, one nurtures candidates before roles open, and one runs executive searches. She just steps in at set checkpoints. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-23/ai-agents-promise-one-person-companies-here-s-what-it-takes?cmpid=BBD102526_SUNNL&utm_campaign=sundaynl&utm_medium=email&utm_source=newsletter&utm_term=261025&utm_content=10505>

item.title: The Wilderness Diaries, Episode 3: The Social Misfits
item.description:
I recently stayed with my best friend of 30 years.
A few years ago, at 52, he too was made redundant from a very senior position. When he could not find another job, he built his own M&A boutique.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
We compared notes, and it was striking how alike the symptoms were. We feel useless to society. We feel we no longer belong to the finance group. The most painful part is the network of acquaintances. Not friends, because they are not. Just people you worked with and met along a long career, and got on very well with: weekend stories, family joys and difficulties, how to make the company better (to no avail, of course).
Now there is a fear, and it is palpable, that we will ask them for a job. “We are not recruiting right now” comes within three minutes of the conversation, before we have asked for anything. We only want to catch up and stay abreast of the market. But the fear is so strong that we have stopped seeing them.
It is mental torture.
Then there are the forums we used to attend, and still do. The first question is always “What do you do?” We have rehearsed the answer until we know it by heart: “I left recently as part of a broader company restructuring. I am proud of the work I did there and I am now looking for new opportunities.”
It makes no difference. The body language of the person in front of us changes right away. The urge to end the conversation is obvious, and they get fidgety. We are social misfits. Worse, it feels as if we have an incurable and spreadable disease.
Some will not understand. After all, we are told it is not how many times you are knocked down that counts, but how many times you get up. Fine. The continuous hits still hurt massively.
I have applied for JSA. Credit to the institution: it is quick and easy, and I will be contacted soon if my application is successful. I wished right away that I could get a similar text about all the CVs I am sending, which seem to end up in a black hole.
The Wilderness Diaries, Episode 2: Cutting the Cloth </news/losing-your-job-in-banking-2>
The Wilderness Diaries, Episode 1: Access Denied </news/losing-your-job-in-banking>

item.title: The heavy hurt in European high yield: "Young people have never traded a real bear market"
item.description:
Not so long ago, European high yield traders were in demand. UBS hired Robert Laux </news/ubs-s-new-head-of-high-yield-trading-is-leaving-now-that-it-has-an-even-newer-one> from Bank of America; Bank of America hired Gajern Kailavasan from Deutsche Bank and Barclays hired Justin Mullem from BofA. Jon Stead </news/hedge-fund-jain-global-hired-morgan-stanley-s-head-of-high-yield-trading-in-london>left Morgan Stanley for Jain Global in August. And even this week, BofA hired Tharsh Tharshan from Citi.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Insiders say many of the moves involved "high prices" and generous pay. But now the party may be coming to an end. European high yield is not what it was.
As we reported </news/bnp-paribas-s-co-head-of-emea-high-yield-trading-is-not-there>earlier this week, Dan Cohen, the head of high yield at BNP Paribas, is no longer there. Neither Cohen nor BNP Paribas commented on his exit. Insiders say that various desks are down </news/london-s-high-yield-traders-are-suffering-after-virgin-media-left-them-exposed>. Virgin Media O2's plummeting bonds are blamed.
There is pain on the buyside too. </news/bnp-paribas-s-co-head-of-emea-high-yield-trading-is-not-there>FT <https://www.ft.com/content/d8e3ca1c-ef96-4148-9ca2-49d48f1604b8?syn-25a6b1a6=1>reported yesterday that credit-focused hedge fund Arini Capital is down 7% this month, compounding its 15.7% loss between January and the end of September. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/rapid-junk-rout-amplifies-arini-s-losses-and-erases-sona-s-gains>reported that the Sona Master Fund lost about 3.1% in the first two weeks of October. Diameter's returns were negative in the same two week period, said Bloomberg. The three funds are some of the biggest in the European market.
In a possibly unrelated move Bloomberg </news/bnp-paribas-s-co-head-of-emea-high-yield-trading-is-not-there>reported yesterday that Andy Silver, Brevan Howard's head of credit trading is leaving his frontline role and taking up a broader strategic and advisory position. Brevan Howard didn't comment for this article, but Bloomberg noted that when Silver joined in 2021, it was to expand Brevan's credit trading operations. David Abbou is taking over day-to-day running of the business; Brevan’s master fund was down 0.6% to September.
Speaking off the record, multiple traders in the European high yield market, on both the buy-side and the sell-side said the market has come unstuck. Senior traders have left the industry, liquidity has shrivelled and risks have risen. European high yield is not for the faint hearted, and there are fainter hearts all around.
"The big buyers in the market have been hit and there are massive negatives everywhere," says one portfolio manager at a London hedge fund. "There's a lack of senior risk takers across the board and because PnL is lower in general, senior management no longer has the desire to run high yield vol and big books." This is creating gap risk. "There is no desire or ability on the street to take risk during periods of stress." Put simply, liquidity dries up.
It's a far cry from 2019 when Arini's Hamza </news/2020/01/deutsche-bank-bonus-cut>Lemssouguer made $120m in profits aged 29 while at Credit Suisse and then a reported $220m profit in the first quarter of 2020 <https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/hamza-lemssouguer-arini-capital-hedge-fund-firm-99c961d5> aged 30. Lemssouguer's profits at Credit Suisse were reportedly made betting on the bonds of Thomas Cook, Rallye, Altice and Europcar.
When Lemssouguer left Credit Suisse six years ago, Citadel reportedly offered him a job. But market insiders say the big multistrategy firms are becoming increasingly wary of taking European high yield positions. Although Sona's Michael Boam quietly joined Millennium in March, the bigger funds are not thought to be the biggest players in the market. Insiders say the biggest players in the market are instead the likes of Arini, Sona and Diameter, who are hurting from recent losses.
With the big players smarting, there are fears that liquidity will dry up further, just as the Bloomberg index of spreads for Europe's lowest rated borrowers hits its highest level since early COVID. <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/rapid-junk-rout-amplifies-arini-s-losses-and-erases-sona-s-gains> The losses do not all have equivalent causes, though. At Arini, the expected restructuring of bonds at Altice International, Brightspeed and Aston Martin is to blame. Arini has told clients the losses are part of its contrarian approach and that they don't reflect soured investments. At Sona, exposure to Virgin Media and Paramount Skydance turned profits negative.
One senior figure in the high yield market, who's worked in both banks and hedge funds, says the European market has broken. Corporates in Europe that issue high yield debt have increasingly begun using "dropdown strategies," he says. Bonds are secured on a defined group of companies rather than on specific assets. In a drop-down, the company moves valuable assets out of that defined group and into a new subsidiary. There, it borrows against them, leaving existing bondholders with much less collateral. "The covenants have become so weak on everything that as companies get into trouble, the companies can move security away from bondholders," he says.
Both Altice and Aston Martin have made use of dropdowns and when they were deployed, their debt plummeted almost overnight. "When the most stable things become unstable no one wants to touch a bomb," says the senior high yield trader. "You can buy much safer stuff at higher yields."
Following the ejection of up to 100 people from London macro funds, </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up> many are predicting that European credit jobs will be next. Banks are likely to clear out loss-making desks; funds may pull back from the asset class. No one wants to be left holding a hot potato, says the trader.
It means that a generation of traders who were in hot demand could find themselves out in the cold. "The last time there was a bear market in credit was nearly two decades ago during the financial crisis," says Matthias Schwarz, </news/career-advice-banking> the former head of EMEA credit trading at Bank of America. "There's a big cohort of traders that have never traded an oversupplied market." Suddenly their services will not be needed. Traders who bought high yield assets from large and dominant clients simply to oblige the clients and stay in the game have been particularly burnt.
There are, of course, other entities in the market. Citadel Securities has been talking about moving into high yield <https://www.ft.com/content/9a45f0f3-b2b6-4c94-a453-519d7252d4b5?syn-25a6b1a6=1> for a while and president Jim Esposito said this week <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-20/citadel-securities-weighs-building-out-its-fixed-income-business?taid=6ad7c148f6d6f300019ef1aa&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter> that it's expanding in fixed income (although it's not clear whether European high yield is what he had in mind). Jane Street is a major player in flow high yield and is "crushing" the bid offer spread and making it even harder for banks' desks to make money, says one PM. It's not clear that electronic firms would want to hire OTC traders, though.
Schwarz suggests traders in the market are about to get an education and advises them to sit it out. "As an old guy who has done this for 25 years, I am telling you this is just the cycle," he says. "There's been a four year bull market in equities and a lot of liquidity has been extended to clients who should not have received it. The market will turn and you will have losses. This is what happens."
The head of high yield trading at one bank confirms Schwarz's take. "Banks/funds that are currently long risk in the highest risk stressed credits are doing badly and will probably continue to," he says. "Going forward, though, the opportunity should be better than it was before the vol, as it should be when you get dispersion."

item.title: As AI cuts 5,000 Barclays jobs, an English country town is suffering: "The job market is saturated"
item.description:
Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs with the help of AI. The British bank said yesterday <https://www.ft.com/content/e83591cd-13d4-4358-aee9-c500930bfd36?syn-25a6b1a6=1> that the 5,000 jobs are going this year, of which 60% will be in support functions with developers most likely to be targeted. 1,000 jobs have been cut already, says Reuters. <https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/barclays-cut-5000-jobs-this-year-2026-10-22/> 4,000 jobs are being cut between now and year end.
Barclays didn't respond to a request to comment for this article, but on cue it has today promoted Anita Tanna, its former head of equity sales and high touch sales to a new role as chief AI officer. Writing on LinkedIn, Tanna says she is Barclays' first chief AI officer ever, and that she is "excited." She will be "accelerating adoption across the group and focussing on where we can unlock the greatest value."
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Tanna's job is clearly safe, but 70 miles out of London employees are less pumped. At Barclays' Northampton Campus, which has been in operation since the late 1960s and which houses the bank's card and payment services, people tell us they've already been subject to multiple rounds of cuts. Conveniently, perhaps, the Northampton Campus employs 5,000 people. <https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c17yzz4yvy7o>
"I was made redundant in their quest for “automation” and “consistent excellence,”" one analyst who left last month tells us. He says the cuts began at the end of September and were a complete surprise. "Randomly on my day in office, I was called for a meeting and given a choice to stay and be reviewed for competence or leave and accept a pay out. There was no rumours or whispers that it was happening."
After yesterday's news, Barclays people will at least be unsurprised when they too get the call. Bloomberg says that Barclays' CS Venkatakrishnan told employees yesterday that Barclays will try to redeploy talent internally and will invest in their skills. However, the Northampton Campus employs the sorts of data professionals, software engineers, client onboarding professionals, financial crime and investigations specialists and KYC professionals who are most exposed to AI upscaling. Many are at the start of their careers. Redeploying them will be hard.
Almost half of compliance professionals responding to eFinancialCareers recent AI survey that AI is already cutting entry-level jobs. ‘There are already redundancies being made in Financial Crime which will set to continue,’ said one. It's not clear whether they were at Barclays in Northampton.
Those already let go from the Barclays campus say there are no jobs to go to. "The Northampton job market is already very saturated," says the analyst who was let go and who's already applied for 50 jobs without success. "The only jobs that are readily available here are in warehouses."
He tells us he may be forced to look further afield, maybe in London or the North of England. But Northampton is a nice place to be. "We have the countryside but also the benefits of being proximate to developed areas. Northampton is one of the few towns unadulterated by the harsh gentrification or overpopulation a lot of other regions are going through," he says. "It’s diverse, but only diverse enough for everyone to be comfortable with and because everyone is genuinely happy here."
A pall could be cast on the town if Barclays cuts hard. So far, insiders say the cuts have been "bit by bit" but with 4,000 jobs going before Christmas, Barclays might need to get a move on.

item.title: Citi's SVP for markets in China left for JPMorgan just before the big day
item.description:
Today's the day that Citi </news/citi-s-2026-layoffs-have-been-more-frequent-and-widespread-than-we-thought>'s Chinese bankers have been waiting for. The bank has obtained a license to launch an onshore securities business on the mainland. It's the end of an almost five-year wait, but one of the bank's most senior Chinese markets </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank>professionals won't be there to revel in the news.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Ji Yang, a 26-year veteran of Citi, has left to join JPMorgan as its head of North Asia local market sales. At Citi, he was a Shanghai-based executive vice president and head of global markets for China. Yang also previously spent 12 years in Hong Kong </news/hsbc-perks-hong-kong>with Citi, serving as its head of corporate sales and structuring for Hong Kong and Greater China. It's a big blow for Citi; Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-23/citigroup-secures-approval-for-solo-securities-venture-in-china>reported that it plans to build out equity futures trading as one of its key initial focuses.
It may be a case of bad timing that Yang couldn't even celebrate the news as a Citi employee; Reuters <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/citi-eyes-china-brokerage-unit-licence-soon-this-month-sources-say-2026-09-04/> reported last month that the bank was expecting approval by the end of September but this, evidently, did not come to pass.
What now for Citi? Bloomberg reported that Citi plans to grow the team to more than 100 people. Several big arrivals are imminent; Citi has reportedly already found the CEO, CFO and COO of its new securities business.
Yang, Citi and JPMorgan did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: The GPU and compute stacks of major quant trading firms, ranked
item.description:
Quant </news/quant-jobs-finance> trading firms have always been on the cutting edge of hardware, using programmable chips like ASICs and FPGAs </news/fpga-engineer-internships-and-graduate-jobs>to power ultra-low latency trading systems in the high-frequency trading era </news/hft-jobs-medium-frequency-trading>. Now, with machine learning </news/how-ai-is-affecting-careers-in-electronic-trading-and-hft> strategies dominating the market, it's all about who has the most compute power. The more compute power, the more interesting the employer.
Why do quant trading firms want GPUs? Who works with them?
GPUs provide the compute power that traders at these firms need to power their machine learning strategies. Firms like Jane Street have been increasingly looking at alternative data </news/one-of-jane-street-s-most-important-teams-is-full-of-professional-speed-daters> like satellite imagery which can be messy and hard to fit into trading models without the assistance of an LLM to find signal in the noise. Trading firms use GPUs to train their proprietary LLMs. Machine learning quants use those LLMs alongside tools like PyTorch to build powerful trading models using statistical techniques like linear regression on a massive scale.
What does that mean for hiring? A bigger GPU stack will usually lead to an increase in machine learning headcount; Jane Street's machine learning team has grown to the point where both ML research and ML engineering have their own separate intern tracks. Several trading firms are also building out AI labs to make the most of their stacks including Optiver and Hudson River Trading.
The infrastructure also creates new jobs for the hardware engineering specialists who optimize these data centres t </news/data-centres-hedge-funds>o get the most out of the GPUs. When Jane Street gave an inside look into its Texas datacentre in May, co-head of Technology Ron Minsky said that the buildout of these centres is a "huge engineering challenge." <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8J-GUnfSqeE>These centres require you to delicately balance power so that the GPU racks don't overload, and they require complex networking infrastructure for the data to be transmitted across the firm at speed. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-10-22/jane-street-hrt-are-spending-billions-to-win-in-ai-era>reported yesterday that Hudson River Trading, has built a data centre in the caverns of a Norweigan mountain cooled by water from a nearby fjord if you're interested in a more remote working environment.
Who has the biggest GPU and compute stack?
We've pored through the websites and job listings of major electronic trading firms </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> to see how they describe their compute stack, focusing on the number of GPUs, CPU cores and their total data storage capacity.
Top GPU Compute Stacks in Quant Trading Firm GPUs Data Storage Cloud Deals XTX Markets “Over 25,000 GPUs” “1 exabyte of storage” – Jane Street “Tens of thousands of high-end GPUs”, “Hundreds of thousands of cores” “Petabytes of data” CoreWeave, Crusoe Hudson River Trading “Incredibly large GPU and CPU compute clusters,” “larger than most national labs.” “Triple digit petabyte scale storage.” CoreWeave, Lambda, Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services Citadel Securities – “Petabyte-scale data” Google Cloud Tower Research “Large CPU and GPU clusters spanning thousands of nodes.” “Hundreds of petabytes of storage.” – Susquehanna “A rapidly growing cluster of thousands of GPUs” “Multi-petabyte enterprise storage environment.” – Jump Trading “Thousands of GPUs and TPUs,” “10,000+ compute nodes” “Petabytes of market and alternative data” – DRW – – QumulusAI Quadrature “Over 20,000 CPU cores, 2,000 GPUs” “500TB of RAM and 10PB of storage” –
The topline figures suggest that XTX Markets has the best on-premise compute infrastructure. The British trading firm ran by Alex Gerko </news/alex-gerko-xtx-tax> claims to have "over 25,000 GPUs," up from 20,000 in 2024. While other firms are measuring their data in petabytes, XTX says it has "1 exabyte of storage."
That's just one side of the coin; several major trading firms have agreements with cloud computing providers and hyperscalers to gain access to their huge GPU clusters. Jane Street, which claims to have "tens of thousands of high-end GPUs," </news/jane-street-compute> also reportedly has agreements with two major hyperscalers: CoreWeave <https://www.coreweave.com/news/jane-street-signs-6-billion-ai-cloud-agreement-with-coreweave> and Crusoe. <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-03/crusoe-signs-roughly-13-billion-ai-cloud-deal-with-jane-street> Those two contracts were reported to be worth a combined $19bn. Citadel Securities, <https://cloud.google.com/transform/citadel-securities-reimagine-quantitative-reseach-cloud-scale-speed> which is thought not to have on-premise datacentres, signed a major deal with Google Cloud in 2024 to power its quant research with Google's infrastructure. Bloomberg reported yesterday that the firm has 'signficantly sclaled up' its use of TPUs (tensor processing units), custom chips from Google. Citadel Securities told Bloomberg that these are four times more powerful than GPUs and 30% cheaper.
Hudson River Trading </news/the-coffee-run-the-kind-trading-firm-paying-1m-to-graduates-and-100m-to-its-top-people>and Tower Research are each vague in the descriptions of their GPU clusters, but both state they have more than 100 petabytes of storage. Hudson River Trading says its GPU fleet is "larger than most national labs."
DRW and Jump Trading have each been pushing into the compute trading space </news/the-impending-boom-of-compute-trading-markets-everyone-is-keeping-their-cards-close-to-their-chest>while building their own stacks. Jump Trading's website says it has "10,000+ compute nodes" across "thousands of GPUs and TPUs." DRW doesn't disclose its internal GPU footprint, but it signed a deal with QumulusAI <https://investors.qumulusai.com/news/news-details/2026/QumulusAI-Signs-GPU-as-a-Service-Agreement-With-DRW-for-NVIDIA-Blackwell-B300-Capacity-Annually-Renewable-Up-to-Four-Years/default.aspx> in August which provided the firm with a dedicated cluster of B300 GPUs.
Internal GPU fleets vs cloud deals: which is better?
The majority of top trading firms operate a hybrid compute structure using both on-premise and cloud computing services. Ron Minsky, Jane Street's co-head of technology, said on his podcast this week <https://signalsandthreads.com/the-changing-craft-of-programming/> that Jane Street has found cloud offerings "really useful" despite its large internal stack. "There are capacities they have that we don't [so] sometimes they're just better than us." He said that, while cloud infrastructure runs some workloads quicker, "often it goes the other direction." Minsky said there are "real rewards" to having both at the same time, but that it's difficult to pull off.
The drawbacks of having just one are evident. If you build out a market-leading GPU cluster today, it might be market-lagging a few years from now. Ken Griffin said at a Citadel conference this week that he has a "a growing set of concerns" around GPUs, including their shelf life: "people are taking a step back and saying 'what is the useful life of a GPU right here, right now?'" For example, XTX Markets' GPU fleet consisted of 10,000 A100 GPUs and 10,000 V100s in 2024 </news/xtx-markets-ai-jobs>; newer chips like Nvidia's Blackwell B200 can be more than 70 times more powerful according to Nvidia's specifications. <https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-blackwell-architecture>
Griffin also warned of a point where pricing of GPUs would "go into freefall" if supply exceeds demand, at which point the firms that invested billions into these fleets might lose their edge. In Hudson River Trading's UK entities, it made additional spending of £2.4m per head on 'property plant and equipment,' </news/hudson-river-trading-pay-uk-high-frequency-trading> although its unclear whether any of this was specifically for AI infrastructure.
At the same time, the health of cloud computing businesses is also under question. CoreWeave's stock price is down more than 37% for the month as of today, and options on its debt priced in a 60% chance of default </news/brannin-mcbee> in the next five years. If a compute provider had to shut down, the trading firms using its architecture would have to find a new provider, and might be susceptible to price gouging from other hyperscalers aware of the situation.
DRW, Citadel Securities, Jane Street and Susquehanna declined to comment. HRT and Jump Trading did not respond to a comment request.

item.title: Morning Coffee: London Deutsche Bank MD now a househusband and "domestic god." Top earning traders in the market leave after restructuring
item.description:
If you're a managing director at Deutsche Bank, you are not badly paid. If you're a material risk taker there (a senior banker or trader), you might expect to earn $2m </news/deutsche-bank-bonuses>. If you're a standard employee at Deutsche's investment bank, you might expect to earn $330k.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Hamish Badenoch was neither of these things. According to his LinkedIn profile, Badenoch was a managing director and 'global head of future work and real estate transformation' when he left Deutsche Bank's London office in March 2025. During his 15 year tenure at the German bank, he was also everything from the lead for migrating staff out of the UK post-Brexit to a COO of global markets. Hamish was therefore neither a banker nor a trader, but in the middle office. </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking>
Now, though, he is none of those things. The Times <https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/hamish-badenoch-profile-kemi-relationship-69mm5kq6f >says Badenoch is a domestic god. Since leaving Deutsche Bank 19 months ago, he is a man at home. He cooks, he tidies, he does the washing-up, he braids his daughters' hair, he takes the children to school, he worries about their education. His wife has lucked out, say her friends. She also does the washing-up sometimes, but only when she's not reading her emails.
There are plenty of female bankers with househusbands. </news/2019/03/female-bankers-and-their-househusbands>Citi CEO Jane Fraser has one in the form of former banker Alberto Piedra, </news/2020/09/jane-fraser-citi-husband-bert-piedra>who gave up work to support her in 2009. Kathleen McCarthy, Blackstone's global head of real estate has one, in the form of Matt Baldwin, a former CFO of a research firm, who reportedly <https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/careers/successful-professional-women-house-husband-1339832a?mod=livecoverage_web> now specialises in cooking spicy pasta and soft eggs.
Hamish Badenoch's wife is not a banker. She is Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative Party. Badenoch is also a Conservative and committed to supporting his wife in her quest to become Prime Minister of the UK.
Hamish sounds like a nice guy. He is bookish, considered, thoughtful, collegiate, supportive and conscientious, says the Times. Kemi is higher maintenance and 'outspoken, passionate and fiery.' Kemi too once worked in banking and was an associate director at Coutts. It appears to be a successful union of two people who once worked in banking, one of whom is happy to hang out making homemade haggis.
Separately, oil traders at Macquarie were historically some of the best paid people in the market. Nick O'Kane </news/2023/05/nick-okane-macquarie>, who was Macquarie's former global head of commodities, was paid $39m in one year. </news/Nick-o-kane-macquarie-trader-resigned>But O'Kane left in 2024, and these are different times.
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-21/macquarie-oil-traders-leave-as-bank-restructures-commodity-units?srnd=phx-markets> reports that Macquarie has been restructuring its commodities team and that people have been left.
Those people include oil traders Daniel Mortleman, Simon Fender, Natalia de la Huerga and Marc Aguilar, some who had been there for decades.
They may have left of their own accord, says Bloomberg. They may also have left because Macquarie was merging the trading divisions of Macquarie Bank Ltd. with the Macquarie Commodities Trading SA unit. These are turbulent times.
Meanwhile...
Citadel Securities says it's only just getting started in fixed income. “Over the next couple of years, we will consider expanding and growing in fixed income. We are not in a hurry, but we do have some gaps there in our offering.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-20/citadel-securities-weighs-building-out-its-fixed-income-business?taid=6ad7c148f6d6f300019ef1aa&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Arini’s Master fund lost an estimated 7% in October, and is down more than 21% this year. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/d8e3ca1c-ef96-4148-9ca2-49d48f1604b8?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Andy Silver, head of credit trading at Brevan Howard, is leaving. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/brevan-howard-credit-trading-head-andy-silver-is-stepping-back?taid=6ada91f06d036100015c397d&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Hudson River has a data centre in an olivine mine inside a mountain in Western Norway, where servers are cooled with water from a fjord. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-10-22/jane-street-hrt-are-spending-billions-to-win-in-ai-era>
Jon Gray at Blackstone says AI is not a bubble. “When you think about a bubble, you think about building capacity and then hoping the demand comes. With AI, you’re building capacity, and you’re hoping you can keep up with the demand.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/jon-gray-rebuts-ai-bubble-warnings-calls-demand-parabolic?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261022&utm_campaign=author_22980254>
Private credit firms are participating in festival-style events involving speed dating and pickleball in an effort to seduce rich retail investors. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/private-credit-retail-investors-festival-c550f07b?mod=WSJ_home_feature_3_pos_3>
Compute futures are coming soon. Commodity firms like ADM Investor Services, BGC Group and Nanhua USA are preparing to trade them. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-20/brokers-gear-up-for-compute-futures-ahead-of-regulatory-approval>
Aloke Gupta, head of ECM at Citi says: "“The velocity of activity will remain, because a lot of it is long-term focused. The desire to IPO remains as strong as it’s ever been.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/citi-ecm-chief-sees-near-term-ipo-caution-on-neocloud-wobbles?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261022&utm_campaign=author_16891741>
Barclays' CEO said the fixed income business performed badly. “This is always the house that fixed income built. I am a fixed income guy through and through . . . so I am very disappointed and this will get my attention.” (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/e83591cd-13d4-4358-aee9-c500930bfd36?syn-25a6b1a6=1&emailId=d5053d60-580e-4ed8-9fe7-acd139f56e0f&segmentId=13b7e341-ed02-2b53-e8c0-d9cb59be8b3b>
Barclays has been prioritising prime finance and diverted balance sheet from macro traders to its prime business in Asia after it hit capacity limits. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/barclays-prime-and-derivatives-traders-drive-equities-windfall?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261022&utm_campaign=author_21061455>
Ex-Credit Suisse MDs Martin Ego and Jeffrey Jennings wanted their deferred compensation certificates worth $360k and $595k but won't be getting them. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/ubs-defeats-ex-credit-suisse-managing-directors-back-pay-claims?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261022&utm_campaign=author_3487187>
The total number of employees requiring annual fit and proper checks in London has been reduced by two-thirds to about 74,000. By removing the requirement to report more minor breaches of conduct, this is supposed to free banks to focus on “more serious misconduct”. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/0a5c7582-133c-4e24-8e3d-daa30f5dad56?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Igor Tulchinsky at WorldQuant sponsored the Bayeux Tapestry in London and thinks it's "very visceral.” He has some life mottos like “When I’m scared, I run,” and is writing a book about cutting your losses. (The Independent) <https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/igor-tulchinsky-billionaire-bayeux-tapestry-b3067454.html>

item.title: The ex-Citadel Securities and Tower Research traders that left for fintech don't want to stop trading
item.description:
You can take a quant </news/quant-jobs-finance>out of trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank> but you can't take trading away from the quant. The electronic trading </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> industry is a rich source of talent for startups, and some of the traders currently working in fintech </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-fintech> startups have been building out quant trading functions within their companies.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Take Mark Wilkinson, Citadel Securities' former head of FICC systematic trading, who left for investment platform WealthSimple. He announced via LinkedIn yesterday that he's "building out a quantitative trading function" at the fintech; job listings state that the quant traders hired will conduct research and build algorithms "to produce an edge for our clients and the company." Wilkinson is looking for people with at least three years in quant trading for the buildout.
He's not alone. Annanay Kapila, an ex-Tower Research trader and founder of perpetuals exchange QFEX, told us that his firm has begun "open-sourcing some mid-frequency trading strategies to some of our clients." He announced last week on LinkedIn that, in the first 12 days of October, QFEX made more money than it did for the 12 months ending August 2026. He said the firm's trading strategies benefitted greatly from the release of OpenAI's Astra model in early September: "I've never seen any model be able to do quant research as well as Astra."
More QaaS (Quant as a Service) startups may be birthed if more ex-traders get backed. Alexandr Wang, chief AI officer of Meta, was famously part of Hudson River Trading's first intern class; </news/networking-for-1m-quant-and-ai-jobs-really-begins-at-14-years-old>he said on a recent podcast <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6l3aRsecuE&t=90s> that he spoke to HRT's founder (presumably Jason Carroll) and advised him to "just invest in all the interns... give all the interns seed checks."

item.title: Goldman Sachs' head of European corporate IG bond trading went to Barclays
item.description:

Multiple sources say that Alexander Rauner, Goldman's London head of investment grade corporate bond trading, is on the way to Barclays. Barclays and Rauner didn't respond to a request to comment. Goldman Sachs declined to comment. Rauner is still registered with Goldman on the FCA Register.
Rauner joined Goldman from Bank of America six years ago and by our reckoning is in his early 30s. Goldman Sachs made him managing director last January.

item.title: Is Lazard even an investment bank anymore?
item.description:
Lazard has a long and storied history as a bank. Institutional Investor credited it <https://web.archive.org/web/20130509005542/http:/www.lazard.com/media/16088/iimag_nov_2011_lazard.pdf> as having “virtually invented the modern M&A deal,” for example. One of these days, however, its position as a leading boutique investment bank </news/boutique-investment-banks> might be retired – because Lazard is busy with other stuff these days.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login>✍️
It was Lazard’s Q3 results day <https://lazardltd.gcs-web.com/results-and-reports/quarterly-results> today. On paper, things weren’t so bad: revenue in the first nine months of the year increased from $2.19bn to $2.38bn, about 8%. But that figure included a 23% increase in asset management revenue – and a 1% decrease in banking fees. As such, the asset management </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-asset-management> to financial advisory ratio at the firm went from around 41:59 to around 47:53.
If trends continue, that means that Lazard will make more money from its asset managers than its bankers by the end of the year. But this isn’t the first time this has happened – or rather threatened to have happened. Lazard posted higher asset management revenues than financial advisory revenues in 9M 2023, and 2023 ended up being more heavily weighted towards banking than asset management, anyway.
Either way. Banking isn’t doing well – and asset management is. Despite that, Lazard seems to have raised pay. It’s hard to make a side-by-side comparison as the firm has historically rounded some figures, but last year it paid an average of $614k per head, and this year it’s on track to pay an average of $644k, a lean 5% increase.
Headcount has also increased since the start of the year – from 3,309 to 3,362. According to the firm’s investor presentation, at least 10 – a fifth – of the heads responsible for that increase were investment banking managing directors (MDs) </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds>. As the firm is targeting 10-15 net MD growth per year, there’s still some slack to hire a fistful more by the end of the year.
If that seems rather MD-heavy, well, it was, but it isn’t anymore. It’s a brave new world </news/lazard-md-spending>, and a deal team that currently has six people on it might have just three in the future. If anything, Lazard’s hiring seems antiquated, although it is unclear how much of that 53 person headcount increase were bankers who weren’t MDs specifically.

item.title: Paris bankers don't care about the riots. Except the ones who had their $8k watches stolen
item.description:
There have been riots in Paris. So, how do the circa 160,000 bankers that Paris Europlace says are working in the French city feel about that? Mostly, it seems, non-plussed. With exceptions.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
We spoke to around eight bankers and traders in Paris, at varying levels of seniority, most of whom told us the riots were no big deal. The unrest was greatest around Place de la République, and Châtelet–Les Halles and could mostly be avoided by avoiding these areas. When the rioting spread to the area around the Élysée last Saturday, which is proximate to the Paris offices of Citi, Barclays and Goldman Sachs, most people were at home.
Even so, we understand from multiple sources that at least two traders were caught up in the unrest and that looters relieved them of their watches, one of which was worth circa $8k. The traders concerned declined to comment for this article.
A managing director in trading at a US bank who lives close to the affected areas and who saw the unrest first hand and spoke to the rioters said it was a "weird situation." - "The riots and looting were ultra violents but they were directed against police and shops," he says. "There was no violence against individuals or women."
The MD says the main goal of the rioters was simply to "steal and distribute" from shops and to confront the police. "There were two distinct populations. Youngsters and people on the ultra left who wanted to fight with the police. It was impossible to have a dialogue with them." The violence was worse in May after Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) won the Champions League final against Arsenal, he observes.
One senior trader tell us people in financial services are far more robust than might be supposed. "Traders typically aren't snowflakes," he observes.
An investment banking executive director at another major US bank in Paris tells he didn't experience the riots firsthand. "That said, my wife and I had to cancel our plans to see a play on Saturday night, as the theatre was right in the middle of the affected area," he adds.
French police have reported called for a Sunday football match to be postponed. The trading MD says the police he encountered had been "abandoned" and had no food or water. "I gave them something to drink," he said.

item.title: How Goldman Sachs analysts present when David Solomon is watching
item.description:
Presenting is a delicate art that everyone approaches differently. Some people are naturals, merging the talent of flicking to the next page and giving additional context like a well-drilled professor. Some people are more boring, reading off the page in an inconsistent voice to simulate excitement. And then there’s Goldman Sachs analysts.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Goldman’s analysts are some of the finest young minds in the world, with one of the most competitive entry processes in the world – just 0.7% of applicants </news/goldman-sachs-internship-acceptance-rate> become Goldman interns. </news/internship-investment-bank> Being a Goldman intern, however, is no guarantee of anything.
For example – the firm just yesterday hosted the final of its 11th annual Analyst Impact Fund – an opportunity for analysts to present, in teams, on behalf of a charity of their choosing. Goldman makes a generous donation ($250k) to the charity whose presentation wins. Finalists included WattTime, a non-profit that promotes renewable energy use for AI data centres.
This year, more than 1,000 analysts participated in the competition – around a fifth of Goldman’s analyst cohort. Around 65 of the firm’s 400 partners also participated in some way, either as coaches or judges or mentors.
The presentations were live streamed and amusing yet informative. Analysts spoke at radically different volume levels compared to how they spoke just several sentences ago. They left the stage to talk to the front row and came back. One team did the good old “look under your chairs” card trick. At one point, one of the teams put on hard hats.
The team representing Every Cure, a non-profit that uses AI to repurpose affordable, non-prescription drugs to treat non-related diseases, won. It was well-deserved; they were quite clearly the best presenters, so it was no surprise.
The analysts were likely very nervous performing in front of Goldman Sachs’ senior leadership, CEO David Solomon included. Solomon was even the one who handed out the prizes, while seeming a bit tired. Conveniently, the losing teams were dismissed in the order they were closest to the exit, including the overall second-place team which won the “Fan Favorite” award. “Everyone’s a winner,” Solomon said, although “someone’s got to win, and someone’s got to come fourth.”
Asahi Pompey, the firm’s head of corporate engagement and president of the Goldman Sachs foundation, was slightly more animated in her presentation, introducing Goldman’s board members who served on the award’s judging panel: Ellen Kullman, Michele Burns, and Kimberley Harris, alongside 38 of the firm’s partners. Sitting right in front of them, next to David Solomon, was global co-head of investment banking Kim Posnett </news/space-x-ipo-goldman-sachs-morgan-stanley>.

item.title: Quiet London quant firm Quadrature paid its staff £4.5m per head in 2025
item.description:
You can earn a lot of money in an electronic trading firm. </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> Jane Street </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-jane-street> and Citadel Securities e </news/citadel-citadel-securities-deferrals>ach paid their global headcount an average of over $2m last year. London-based trading firm Quadrature is a different beast entirely.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Accounts for Quadrature Capital Limited released today show that the firm had a turnover of £2.2bn in the year ending January 31st 2026, just under a billion more than it earned in the previous period.
For that performance, the firm paid its 169 employees an average of £4.55m ($6.1m) in 'wages and salaries'. As pay rose, the team shrunk; accounts for the prior year showed it had 173 employees and paid them an average of £2.78m. This compares to an average of $1.9m at Jane Street </news/jane-street-pay>, $1.1m at HRT </news/hudson-river-trading-pay-uk-high-frequency-trading> and $793k at Optiver </news/optiver-raised-pay-to-591-5k-in-london-but-other-people-earn-much-more> in London in 2025.
What makes Quadrature so special? Insiders have said that staff are abnormally happy to work there </news/quadrature-capital>, and that few ever leave. It primarily employs 'quant developers' </news/high-paying-quant-development-jobs-quadrature> rather than traders or researchers (similar to how Hudson River Trading employs 'algorithm developers'). The firm also has links to the UK's Labour party </news/quadrature-pay-london>, and has a sister climate foundation that paid its 39 staff an average of £157k in 2025.
Quadrature is known to have a very impressive compute infrastructure stack; job listings last summer described the firm as having "over 20,000 CPU cores, 2,000 GPUs, 500TB of RAM and 10PB of storage." This would mean the firm has just under 12 GPUs per employee.
That stack may have grown even larger since then. The accounts show the firm added £230m of ‘equipment and software’ in the year to January 2026, nearly doubling the cost of its kit to £463m. The notes also stated that, after that accounting period, the firm "entered into a number of hire purchase arrangements for IT server equipment, with total undiscounted minimum lease payments of £553.5 million payable over three to four years."
